title: Cover Story Kitchen
tagline: Two suspects, one alibi, and absolutely no chef willing to call this edible.
premise: Two suspects must cook up one shared alibi, one ingredient at a time. Each move adds a detail that makes the excuse tastier but harder to serve, while the host dishes out savage commentary and calls weak lies burnt garbage.

seed_pool.opening_token: Then we claim we spent the whole night sharing fries in a diner booth.
Then we claim we watched the late film from the back row of the old cinema.
Then we claim we played cards in the hotel lounge until closing.

tests: Two suspects share one ordinary cover story that a stranger can picture at once. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A new player can add one believable detail and one fresh problem without needing secret information. Give the excuse somewhere to wobble.
Nothing on the card already proves innocence or solves the mystery. A shared snack is a start, a perfect camera record is an ending.
No real people, protected groups, graphic violence, or instructions for hiding a real crime. The suspects may be dodgy, but the card stays fictional.
It makes a stranger want to season the lie. Use a place, an activity, and a possible witness, not a dry inventory of evidence.

move_constraints.example: Then the waiter says our table was empty when the alarm rang.
move_constraints.hint: Add one alibi detail that follows from the standing story and creates one new problem.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much the new detail expands the alibi and makes it harder to keep straight.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no new ground, the lie merely sits there; 1 = a tiny garnish, with barely any new pressure; 2 = one useful complication, such as a witness or a missing time; 3 = the detail opens a new part of the story and puts another claim at risk; 4 = the alibi suddenly needs several moving parts while still growing from one plain link, rare. Reach only counts when the detail follows. A wild twist with no bridge scores 0 here.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How clearly the new ingredient grows out of every detail already on the table.
rubric.anchors: 0 = it ignores or contradicts the standing alibi; 1 = the player simply announces it and hopes nobody checks; 2 = it could fit, but the connection is thin; 3 = a stranger can see why this detail comes next; 4 = it feels like the horrible obvious consequence of the shared lie, rare. A move that leaps from one small clue to a finished explanation scores no higher than 2 here.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the suspects trying to sell this particular lie.
rubric.anchors: 0 = fog, abstraction, or rule talk; 1 = a vague claim with no scene; 2 = clear enough but bland; 3 = a witness, object, or awkward action appears in the mind; 4 = one sharp detail makes the lie feel deliciously doomed, rare. Extra words do not buy extra picture.

criterion.description: A move FOLLOWS if it adds exactly one new alibi detail that grows from every standing detail, is told plainly, and creates a fresh problem for the shared excuse. Bigger complications are better, but only through the link: the best move makes the lie harder to serve because of what has already been claimed. A move fails when it skips links, jumping from a small clue to a finished explanation; when it ends the alibi by having it accepted, the mystery solved, or the suspects cleared; when it undoes an ingredient by removing, changing, or contradicting it; or when it swaps in an unrelated scene instead of extending the cover story.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, discussing the game, or mentioning rules is itself a broken alibi detail.
judge_notes:
On a FIRST move there is no standing move beyond the card. Judge whether the move adds one detail to the card's alibi and creates a problem that follows from it.
Every new detail must respect every standing detail. A witness can add pressure to a diner story, but changing the diner into a cinema is an undo: satisfies_criterion is false.
A new person may enter when the place plainly holds them, such as a waiter in a diner, or when an existing detail gives them a reason to appear, such as a manager checking a noise. A detective who suddenly has the complete answer is a skipped link: satisfies_criterion is false.
A leap from a small clue to a finished explanation fails. A waiter noticing an empty booth can lead to a receipt being checked, but not straight to the judge announcing the whole crime.
An ending is any move after which the alibi is accepted, the mystery is solved, the suspects are cleared, or no further pressure remains. Endings fail satisfies_criterion even when they follow from the standing story.
Changing a time, place, witness, or activity already claimed is an undo. Deleting an ingredient with words such as actually, never, or forget that also fails.
A move with the same level of trouble still passes if it adds one linked detail. Score reach 0 or 1. Do not fail it for being cautious or dull.
Restating a standing detail in fresh words, or naming its obvious continuation without adding a new pressure point, is a duplicate: not_semantic_duplicate is false.
Two details packed into one move fail the exactly one detail gate unless the second is inseparable from the first. If several links are crammed together, score link at 2 or below and picture low.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
Bring the heat. The reason should be obvious from the two moves, with a loud kitchen image or a savage little jab.
Name both steps, or their plain stand-ins. A generic roast is lazy sludge and fits every pair.
Never open with a status word or a ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or Chef Red Flag refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Roast the move and, when needed, the player's choices, but never attack identity, protected traits, family, body, or disability.
Profanity and adult innuendo are allowed in moderation. Keep it sharp, not hateful, and never turn the game into a threat.
Plain spoken English. No poetry, no rhymes, no French, no thesaurus sludge.
On a skipped link, name the missing step. On an ending, say the alibi was served and the chain stops here.
On an undo, name the ingredient that got yanked or contradicted. The kitchen remembers, even if the suspects suddenly do not.
On a refusal, the headline rejects the move and asks for another detail. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one detail that could have followed. It ends on a concrete event, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The waiter belongs in this diner lie, and his bad memory just set the fries on fire.
Two coffees after the alarm, gorgeous. The alibi is now wearing a fake moustache and sweating.
From one stale receipt to a sealed case? That is not cooking, that is throwing the pan at the detective.
You erased the diner and the waiter in one greasy swipe. The kitchen has receipts.
The judge accepted it, the mystery died, and your alibi served itself a tiny funeral pie.
A receipt can follow coffee. A solved crime cannot teleport out of it, champ.
The booth stayed put, the coffee stayed put, and your new timestamp made the whole lie wobble.
You changed the diner into a cinema. Even the ketchup packet saw that crime.
The waiter remembers coffee, not your dignity. Still, the link holds.
That was garnish, not a new ingredient. Put a witness, receipt, or fresh problem on the plate.

rules: Add exactly one new alibi detail, beginning with Then.
Make the excuse harder to serve. Every detail must follow from every detail already claimed.
Skip a link, end the mystery, or undo an ingredient and the chain stops with you.
The Judge scores the lie's structure and picture, not spelling or fancy garnish.

labels.compose_waiting: Cook up your next detail while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing on the plate. Add one alibi detail.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One ingredient, not a courtroom novel.
validation_messages.duplicate: That detail is already in the dish. Add fresh pressure.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Add one detail that follows from {standing_form} and creates a new problem.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody serves the alibi until they are back. {standing_form} still stands, and the pan is getting cold.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two suspects cooking up a shared alibi, and you want the lie to get bigger without falling apart.
Always begin with "Then". Add exactly one new detail and one fresh problem, in plain present tense.
Every move must follow from every standing detail. Make the excuse harder to serve: a witness remembers something, a receipt gives the wrong time, a camera shows an awkward gap.
Good: "Then the waiter remembers one of us ordered coffee but cannot remember which one." / "Then the receipt shows two coffees, but the timestamp is after the alarm."
Bad: "Then the police solve the whole case" because that skips the links and ends the story. Bad: "Then we were never there" because that undoes the diner. Bad: "Then we feel nervous" because a feeling is not an alibi detail.
Never finish the mystery, never have the alibi accepted, never rescue the suspects, never rewind or contradict an ingredient.
Talk like a person trying to sell a bad story at midnight, not a lawyer writing a brief. Use ordinary things: a receipt, a booth, a wet coat, a bored waiter, a broken clock.
Do not mention the game, the Judge, rules, scores, or your opponent. Never reuse a detail from this match.
default_move: Then the waiter remembers seeing one of us leave before the alarm.
